security_privacy_cost_impact: No provider, credential, network, data or cost. Tightens the fakes and helpers: an outbox append now refuses an event whose tenant context differs from the unit's minted one in any field (not only workspace); the relay limits and three domain helpers read a caller's value once; a re-entrant consume is refused instead of hanging; enqueue refuses attempts or timeouts above the kernel caps so a crashed worker's job is not unreclaimable for an unbounded time; handlers get an abort signal at timeout. Every new refusal is a constant TypeError message or a minted code, carrying nothing thrown. A1 reads it (risk lane).
migration_and_data_impact: None: no migration, no db/** change; the code is not wired to app.jobs, app.outbox_events or app.consumer_ledger (the adapter is scope.exclude).
compatibility_impact: Narrowing within the kernel's fakes and helpers, no contract change: JobHandler gains a second parameter (an AbortSignal) that one-parameter handlers ignore; enqueue rejects above the D6 caps; append refuses a context that is not the unit's own; consumeEvent returns failed for a re-entrant call; refOf reports a throwing read as its constant TypeError. Nothing outside platform-kernel imports these yet (index.ts and run.ts unchanged). No contract-catalog, dependency or tool-configuration change.
known_limitations: The re-entry guard sees one process's async call chain (AsyncLocalStorage); a handler that hands the event to another process and waits on it there is outside it, as the database's own lock wait would be.
The abort signal is advice: a handler that ignores it may still overlap a reclaiming worker after the back-off; at-least-once stays the documented contract.
The cap values are D6 test values, owed with the other D6 limits.
